headline: AI agents are now learning reusable diffraction skills and accelerating materials simulations.
summary_for_scientists: A self-learning X-ray diffraction agent turns analysis experience into skills it validates before reuse, and AtomWorld-Mirror reports large speedups for long-horizon atomistic simulation. New work also tests open-ended scientific rediscovery, diffraction-to-structure retrieval, and closed-loop catalyst experiments.

lab_pick.title: A self-learning scientific agent improves X-ray diffraction analysis
lab_pick.what_they_did: Gan Jiang diagnoses failures in powder X-ray diffraction analyses, revises executable skills, and validates those skills before reusing them.
lab_pick.result: The paper reports top-1 accuracy of 96.30% on MP500 and 81.78% on RRUFF without supplied composition, and leading evaluated results on DeltaXRDbench.
lab_pick.why_researchers_care: The system turns analytical experience into reusable, testable procedures rather than relying only on a longer prompt. Its examples span phase identification, multiphase analysis, battery lattice evolution, and catalyst configurations.
lab_pick.how_to_share: Use a lab-meeting demo: choose one public diffraction sample, inspect the agent's skill and result, then compare it with a human analyst's workflow.
